chapters.title: Agent states
chapters.subtitle: Why an agent is not taking work

steps.text: Agent states are the reasons an agent gives when they are not taking work: lunch, a meeting, training. This video shows why they exist, how to create a reason code, and what agents see in their presence menu.
When agents are not taking work, a manager needs to know why. An agent at lunch is not the same as an agent who is stuck with a system problem.
A reason code gives the agent a name to pick, such as Lunch, Team meeting or Training. Each one belongs to one of the built-in presence states.
Reports and the Live dashboard then show both the state and the reason, so nobody has to ask.
A reason code has a name, and the state it applies to: Break, Away, Do not disturb, Meeting, Training, or After-hours unavailable.
A sort order decides where it appears in the presence menu. A lower number appears higher.
The site starts with seven reason codes. You can change them, delete them, and add your own.

chapters.title: Create a reason code
chapters.subtitle: A name, a state and a position

steps.text: Open Interaction Center, Management, Agent states. The list shows each reason code with the state it applies to. Click Add reason code.
Type a Name, such as Customer visit, and an optional Description.
Choose the state it Applies to. A visit away from the desk is a Meeting.
Set a Sort order. Lower numbers appear higher in the presence menu. Leave Enabled ticked, and click Save.
Agents change their state from the presence menu on My workspace. The same menu is in the Contact Center bar at the bottom of every admin page.
Available is always listed. Every reason code that is not a break is listed on its own, and sets the state right away. The new Customer visit is among them.
Break reasons are grouped under a Break heading, here Short break and Lunch.
To stop offering a reason, open it and untick Enabled, then click Save.
A disabled reason code is hidden from the presence menu, but it stays on historical records, so past reports still make sense.
When an agent is busy on a call, the Break heading reads Request break. The break starts as soon as the current work ends.
If no reason codes exist at all, the menu falls back to the plain states: Away, Do not disturb, Meeting, Training and After-hours unavailable.
The starting codes are Short break and Lunch, Away from desk, Team meeting, Coaching, Training and System issue.
Separating lunch from short breaks, so reports show the real length of each.
A Coaching code, so supervisors know an agent is in a review and not idle.
A System issue code, to see how much time a tooling problem costs.
A code for after-hours unavailability, for agents who work a split shift.
Create the reasons your team needs, and agents pick one when they step away. Reports and the dashboard show the rest. Thanks for watching.
